title: Heritage sites in Telangana: Ramappa, Warangal and Golconda
seo_title: Heritage Sites in Telangana: Ramappa, Warangal and Golconda
meta_description: Heritage sites in Telangana: the UNESCO Ramappa Temple, Warangal Fort, the Thousand Pillar Temple, Golconda, the Qutb Shahi tombs and Charminar.
summary: Telangana's UNESCO World Heritage Site is the Ramappa (Kakatiya Rudreshwara) Temple at Palampet, inscribed in 2021. Around it lie the Kakatiya capital of Warangal with its fort and Thousand Pillar Temple, and in Hyderabad the Qutb Shahi city of Golconda, the Qutb Shahi tombs and Charminar. Buddhist sites such as Nelakondapalli and Phanigiri and the megaliths of the Deccan add older layers.

paras: Telangana sits on the Deccan plateau, and its history follows the great Deccan powers. Megalithic burials, including stone circles, survive at many sites. Under Satavahana and Ikshvaku rule, Buddhist stupas and monasteries flourished in the Krishna valley in the early centuries CE. From the 12th century to 1323 the Kakatiyas ruled from Hanamkonda and later Warangal, building temples, forts and tanks. After them came the Bahmanis, the Qutb Shahis of Golconda and finally the Asaf Jahi Nizams of Hyderabad.

Each layer left a distinct architecture, so a short trip can cover star-shaped temples, a circular fort, royal tombs and an 18th to 20th century palace city. Our explainer on [indo-islamic architecture](indo-islamic-architecture.html) helps with the later monuments.

The Ramappa temple at Palampet, in Mulugu district, was begun in 1213, in the reign of the Kakatiya ruler Ganapatideva, by his general Recherla Rudra. It was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2021. It stands on a raised star-shaped platform, and its bracket figures of maidens and mythical beasts are carved in hard dolerite. The temple's tower is built with light, porous 'floating' bricks that reduce the weight of the roof structure.

The temple is still part of a working landscape: the large Ramappa lake nearby is a Kakatiya-built reservoir. Our lecture [Deccan temple forms and Vesara debates](deccan-temple-forms-vesara-debates.html) explains where Kakatiya temples fit in the story of Deccan architecture.

Warangal Fort had concentric circular walls of earth and stone, and at its centre stand four carved stone gateways, the Kakatiya Kala Thoranam. The Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda, of the 12th century, is a triple shrine with a richly carved pillared hall. Nearby are the Bhadrakali temple beside its lake and the Kakatiya temple group at Ghanpur.

A day in Warangal paired with Ramappa makes a strong study visit for architecture students. Our session on [temple inscriptions and patrons](temple-inscriptions-patrons.html) uses Kakatiya inscriptions to show who paid for temples and why.

sections.h2: Hyderabad: Golconda, the tombs and Charminar
paras: Golconda Fort, on a granite hill in western Hyderabad, grew under the Qutb Shahi kings from the 16th century into a fortified city known for its acoustics, a clap at the entrance being said to carry to the summit. Below it lie the Qutb Shahi tombs, a royal necropolis of domed tombs and mosques now restored with gardens and stepwells.

The Charminar, completed in 1591, stood at the heart of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah's new city of Hyderabad, with the Mecca Masjid, Chowmahalla Palace and the Salar Jung Museum nearby. See our [Hyderabad heritage walk guide](heritage-walk-in-hyderabad.html) for routes through the old city.

Nelakondapalli in Khammam district has the remains of a large Buddhist stupa and monastery. Phanigiri, in Suryapet district, has yielded fine sculpture of the Ikshvaku period. Kondapur, near Sangareddy, is an early historic site. Megalithic burials, including stone circles, are found in the state, and our lecture on [burials and bioarchaeology](burials-and-bioarchaeology.html) explains how they are studied.

faq.q: What is the UNESCO World Heritage Site in Telangana?
faq.a: The Ramappa Temple, officially the Kakatiya Rudreshwara Temple, at Palampet in Mulugu district. Begun in 1213, it was inscribed in 2021 for its architecture, sculpture and its place in a Kakatiya landscape of tanks and fields.

faq.q: What are the main historical places in Hyderabad?
faq.a: Golconda Fort, the Qutb Shahi tombs, Charminar, the Mecca Masjid, Chowmahalla Palace and the Salar Jung Museum. Together they cover the Qutb Shahi and Nizam periods.

faq.q: What is special about the Thousand Pillar Temple?
faq.a: It is a 12th century Kakatiya temple at Hanamkonda, a triple shrine raised on a star-shaped platform and richly carved.

faq.q: Are there Buddhist sites in Telangana?
faq.a: Yes. Nelakondapalli, Phanigiri and Dhulikatta are among the main Buddhist sites.
